description.from:
KDATAP-d6eabf rules that display names are never identity inputs and that `subject.name` may not rescue a key mismatch. Agreed for matching. But `subject.name` is not the same field on every layer, and the gold loader cannot be written until it is told which.

| layer | populated | what it actually holds |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| mentions | 339 of 357 differ from the key | the **source token observed**: `pii:access_token`/`id_token`, `pii:user_identifier`/`sub`, `pii:credential_secret`/`refresh_token` |
| components (asset) | 473 of 473 | a code instance: `directus_users`, `LocalAuthDriver`, `UsersService`, `appSession` |
| components (third_party) | 52 of 52 | the vendor: `Auth0`, `Stripe`, `SendGrid` |
| data flows | 436 of 436 | prose restating the key: `flow:oidc-callback->session` / "OIDC callback to session" |

**Proposed decision.** Mentions: promote into the canonical source-name field. This is the same source-name-versus-inferred-concept separation KDATAP-d6eabf already calls for on data items; mention gold records both, the source name is simply in the wrong field. Assets and actors: evidence/display, not the canonical instance (see the component instance ruling). Flows: discard.

**Why it cannot be a blanket rule.** Dropping all display names destroys the only record of what was observed on 339 annotations, and it is the field that makes the remaining adjudication possible — `pii:email_address` named `clientID` is very likely a mislabel and is only visible because the source token was kept.

Rejected: a single global rule; keeping `subject.name` as a matching token anywhere.
description.to:
KDATAP-d6eabf rules that display names are never identity inputs and that `subject.name` may not rescue a mismatch. The loader still needs a lossless, per-layer migration rule.

Measured legacy shape:

| layer | legacy name content |
| --- | --- |
| mentions | 339 of 357 differ from the key; often the observed source token |
| data items | 61 of 436 differ from the key; often casing, accessor, or alternate source spelling |
| components: asset/actor | code-level name or display text |
| components: third party | usually the asserted vendor |
| data flows | prose restating the legacy key |

**Proposed decision.**

- Mentions and data items: preserve `subject.name` as an `observedTokenCandidate` with provenance. Do not promote it automatically to authoritative source identity or concept. Validate it against evidence and adjudicate discrepancies such as `pii:email_address` / `clientID`.
- Assets and actors: preserve as observed code/display evidence, not a required canonical instance.
- Third parties: preserve as a vendor candidate and validate it against the asserted canonical vendor.
- Flows: retain only as legacy migration provenance; it is not a canonical endpoint or matching field.

No layer may use the candidate or display value to rescue identity. Canonical source identity and concept fields are populated only after mechanical validation or human adjudication.

Rejected: a single global rule; dropping potentially useful observed text; blindly promoting all names; keeping `subject.name` as a matching token.
